game_info.title: Traveller Roleplaying Game Rules
game_info.description: Core rules from Traveller including character creation, combat, and subsector trading.

character_creation.description: Traveller character creation is a unique process where characters age during service, gaining skills, wealth, and potentially injuries or death.

endurance.description: Health, stamina, and resistance to damage.

careers.description: Characters serve in various careers for 2-6 terms of 5 years each. Each term provides skill training, wealth, and potential injuries.

available_careers.name: Pirate
available_careers.description: Space piracy and raiding (new in Traveller Companion 2024).

available_careers.name: Scholar
available_careers.description: Academic research and study (new in Traveller Companion 2024).

available_careers.name: Outfit
available_careers.description: Corporate and mercenary organizations (new in Traveller Companion 2024).

skill_training.description: Each career term provides skill training. Characters roll 2D6 and consult the career's skill training table.

skill_types.general: Available to all characters, based on attributes.
skill_types.career: Specific to the career, learned during service.
skill_types.bonus: Extra skills learned through duty performance or special events.

skill_modifiers.description: Skill checks use the skill level + attribute modifier vs a target number.

wealth.description: Characters earn wealth during each career term based on rank and duty performance. Wealth is spent at the end of each term.
wealth.wealth_table: 2D6 x 1,000 credits per die, based on rank

mustering_out.description: When a character leaves a career, they receive mustering-out benefits based on their reason for leaving.

benefits.honorable_discharge: Full pension, bonus wealth, and possible ship or vehicle.
benefits.retirement: Full pension, bonus wealth, and possible ship or vehicle.
benefits.death: Character dies during service, create a new character.

new_2024_benefits: Extended service bonuses for longer terms
Bonus skills for exceptional duty performance

combat_rules.description: Traveller combat uses a d20 system with initiative, movement, and attack resolution.

initiative.description: Each combatant rolls 2D6 + DEX modifier. Highest goes first, ties go to the attacker.
initiative.combat_rounds: Each round represents 5 seconds of combat.

movement.description: Characters can move up to their movement allowance (based on STR and END) each round.

attack_resolution.description: Attack rolls use 2D6 + skill level + attribute modifier vs a target number.

damage.description: Damage is tracked in terms of hit points. When hit points reach zero, the character is incapacitated.

injuries.description: Severe damage can cause injuries that impair the character.
types: Wounded: -3 to all rolls, cannot take actions

ship_combat.description: Ship combat is resolved in a series of impulses, with each ship taking turns to move and fire.
ship_combat.impulses: Each turn is divided into 12 impulses. Ships move based on their thrust rating.

thrust.description: Ship thrust is measured in Gs. Higher thrust means faster acceleration.
thrust.movement: Ships accelerate at their thrust rating each impulse.

missile.range: Long range, travel time based on distance

pdd.description: Point Defense Devices intercept incoming missiles.

hit_locations.description: Ships have hit locations that correspond to different parts of the ship.
locations: Life Support: Ship atmosphere and pressure

subsector_trading.description: Subsector trading is a core activity in Traveller. Characters buy and sell goods between worlds to make a profit.

trade_goods.description: Trade goods vary by world type and availability. Prices fluctuate based on supply and demand.

world_types.description: Worlds are classified by their environment and development level, which affects trade goods availability.

types.name: Agricultural
types.price_modifier: Food is cheaper, other goods are more expensive

types.name: Industrial
types.price_modifier: Manufactured goods are cheaper, other goods are more expensive

types.name: Commercial
types.description: Worlds focused on trade and commerce.
types.price_modifier: Prices are stable, trade is profitable

types.name: Tourist
types.description: Worlds focused on tourism and leisure.
types.price_modifier: Luxury goods are cheaper, other goods are more expensive

trade_mechanics.description: Trading involves buying goods at one world and selling them at another for a profit.

steps.name: Assess Market
steps.description: Determine the availability and prices of goods at the current world.

steps.name: Buy Goods
steps.description: Purchase goods at the current world's prices.

steps.name: Travel
steps.description: Travel to another world, paying for fuel and maintenance.

steps.name: Sell Goods
steps.description: Sell goods at the new world's prices.

steps.name: Calculate Profit
steps.description: Profit = Selling Price - Buying Price - Travel Costs

price_modifiers.description: Prices are modified by world type, government, and law level.

government.feudal: Prices are higher due to lack of competition
government.democracy: Prices are stable due to free market
government.autocracy: Prices are controlled by the government
government.anarchy: Prices are volatile due to instability

law_level.high: Prices are higher due to regulation
law_level.low: Prices are lower due to lack of regulation
law_level.none: Prices are volatile due to lawlessness

ship_requirements.description: Trading requires a ship with sufficient cargo capacity and jump capability.
ship_requirements.cargo_capacity: Measured in tons, determines how much can be carried.
ship_requirements.jump_capability: Determines how far the ship can travel in one jump.
ship_requirements.fuel_capacity: Determines how many jumps can be made without refueling.
ship_requirements.crew_requirements: Minimum crew based on ship size and complexity.

starship_design.description: Starships are designed using a point-based system. Each ship has a hull, engines, life support, power plant, and computer.

hull.description: The physical structure of the ship. Determines cargo capacity and armor.
hull.size: Measured in tons, determines the ship's size.

engines.description: Ship propulsion. Determines thrust and maneuverability.

types.maneuvering: For movement within a star system.
types.jump: For faster-than-light travel between star systems.

life_support.description: Maintains atmosphere and pressure. Determines how many crew can be supported.
life_support.rating: Based on the number of crew and passengers.

power_plant.description: Generates energy for the ship's systems and weapons.
power_plant.rating: Based on the ship's energy requirements.

computer.description: Controls navigation, weapons, and other systems.

patrol.description: Multi-purpose ships designed for patrol and escort.
